assets.title: 泡泡乐园｜认识题材
assets.prompt:
Create ONE complete portrait 9:16 mobile casual game BATTLE SCREEN concept, approximately 1080x1920, full screen edge to edge, no phone frame. Original game concept: a squad of mischievous bubble creatures defend their home from a descending, dense colorful bubble mosaic. This is a polished actual playable-screen mockup, not a poster, character lineup, level-selection map or multi-panel collage.

ART DIRECTION: premium cheerful 2D casual game illustration with plump, clearly drawn original characters, clean warm-dark colored outlines, controlled cel shading and soft bright highlights. Juicy solid main colors. Soap-bubble targets have a small shiny highlight and a slightly iridescent rim but a mostly OPAQUE strong color center for legibility. Creature bodies look like expressive cartoon bubble beings, not realistic plastic toys. No realistic textures. Soft cream, aqua and lavender world accents, subtle decorative foam at the outer margins. The mood is playful and energetic, with visible impact and squash-and-stretch. The battlefield background is subdued and uncluttered so every target color is readable.

CORE GAMEPLAY MUST BE VISIBLE: player chooses colored creatures from four waiting queues; several deployed creatures automatically SPIT matching colored bubble projectiles upward; each attacks only same-color target bubbles. Three same-color creatures can fuse into a stronger one. The enemy bubble mosaic slowly presses downward toward a horizontal defense boundary. Removing individual targets opens gaps and intact bubbles above FALL into those gaps; falling bubbles are not automatically destroyed. Preserve this as squad deployment and rapid automatic shooting, not a traditional manual-aim bubble cannon.

SCREEN LAYOUT, all three scenes of the same game must share this layout:
- Top 0-9%: small pause button upper left, compact Chinese level label, slim progress bar with percentage. No shop, energy counters, star rating or extra game modes.
- Upper battlefield 10-58%: a very dense, tightly packed grid-like mosaic of SMALL colored bubble beads, approximately FIFTY TO SIXTY beads across, hundreds to thousands of tiny units forming ONE large recognizable pixel-art picture. Use a few contiguous flat color regions, not random rainbow confetti. Never draw only 8-12 giant bubbles across as in an ordinary bubble shooter. This mosaic is the largest visual mass on screen.
- Defense boundary near 59%: a thin luminous foam rail, clearly separating targets from allies. Keep its frontline visible.
- Active squad row around 61-70%: EXACTLY SEVEN small deployment pads on a single baseline; FIVE visibly occupied, TWO empty. Characters face upward toward the target grid with expressive 3/4 faces still visible. Small legible remaining-shot counters on badges at their feet, e.g. 96, 58, 318, 402, 233. Pads are simple softly rounded colored soap rings, not flowerpots. Creature bodies dominate their silhouette; their main color must match their projectile and target color.
- Bottom waiting area around 73-89%: exactly FOUR vertical queue lanes, each with THREE much smaller waiting bubble creatures. Frontmost creature is nearest the deployed row. Small remaining-shot numbers and subtle front-row selection corners. This must be visibly a queue, not a card deck or inventory.
- Bottom 91-99%: THREE compact readable rounded buttons with icons and exact Chinese labels: 重排 (shuffle arrows), 优先出战 (forward arrow), 泡泡炸弹 (a small bubble burst icon). Keep the whole game screen visible.

CONSISTENT ORIGINAL CAST: blue #2982F4 round puff with two tiny cheek fins and little feet, big eyes and inflated cheeks; orange #FF7E27 pear-shaped creature with two short rounded horn nubs and a mischievous grin; green #30D183 squat puffy creature with three short soft back bumps, no leaves; purple #B672FD bean-shaped creature with two floppy ear nubs and a broad elastic mouth; yellow #FFDF48 soft rounded-cube creature with two tiny antennae and cheerful face; red #FF525B little inverted-heart creature with a small quiff and energetic determined face. Optional white #FFFFFF round pill creature outlined in cool gray. Each is mostly one main color, tiny simple appendages, no clothes, armor, handheld weapons or large accessories. They visibly inhale, inflate cheeks and spit bubbles with elastic recoil. No generic smiling circles alone: each silhouette and mouth shape has personality.

AVOID: plants, flowers, leaves, vegetables, pots, farm fences, military aircraft, zombies, copied recognizable franchise characters, branded bubble dragons or logos, realistic guns, a single central player cannon, aiming guide lines, finger gesture overlays, match-three exchange arrows, a win popup, tutorial text, extra UI panels, photographic rendering, watermark. All Chinese UI must be crisp and readable.

SCENE 1 — SUNNY BUBBLE PLAYGROUND. A bright sky-island home, with pale warm-blue clouds and just a few whimsical inflated arch shapes at the far screen edges. The center remains a calm light blue-gray playfield. Top label 第 12 关, progress 35%. The dense bubble mosaic depicts a large cheerful yellow rubber duck on blue water, with orange beak and white/light-blue surrounding areas, in bead-pixel art. Its lower edge is being nibbled away by accurate same-color attacks. FIVE active creatures in left-to-right colors blue, orange, yellow, purple and white, with two empty pads interspersed. Show two or three short distinct same-color projectile streams, inflated cheeks, one creature recoiling after a spit, and only a few small local pop ripples at actual impacts. Avoid overwhelming effects: the priority is instantly understanding the creatures, matching colors, the huge bubble picture, the seven pads and four waiting queues. A few displaced intact beads fall through a small gap. Overall feel: welcoming, lively, easy to play, a coherent bubbly world.

Three same-color creatures can fuse into a stronger one. The enemy bubble mosaic slowly presses downward toward a horizontal defense boundary. Removing individual targets opens gaps and intact bubbles above FALL into those gaps; falling bubbles are not automatically destroyed. Preserve this as squad deployment and rapid automatic shooting, not a traditional manual-aim bubble cannon.

SCREEN LAYOUT, all three scenes of the same game must share this layout:
- Top 0-9%: small pause button upper left, compact Chinese level label, slim progress bar with percentage. No shop, energy counters, star rating or extra game modes.
- Upper battlefield 10-58%: a very dense, tightly packed grid-like mosaic of SMALL colored bubble beads, approximately FIFTY TO SIXTY beads across, hundreds to thousands of tiny units forming ONE large recognizable pixel-art picture. Use a few contiguous flat color regions, not random rainbow confetti. Never draw only 8-12 giant bubbles across as in an ordinary bubble shooter. This mosaic is the largest visual mass on screen.
- Defense boundary near 59%: a thin luminous foam rail, clearly separating targets from allies. Keep its frontline visible.
- Active squad row around 61-70%: EXACTLY SEVEN small deployment pads on a single baseline; FIVE visibly occupied, TWO empty. Characters face upward toward the target grid with expressive 3/4 faces still visible. Small legible remaining-shot counters on badges at their feet, e.g. 96, 58, 318, 402, 233. Pads are simple softly rounded colored soap rings, not flowerpots. Creature bodies dominate their silhouette; their main color must match their projectile and target color.
- Bottom waiting area around 73-89%: exactly FOUR vertical queue lanes, each with THREE much smaller waiting bubble creatures. Frontmost creature is nearest the deployed row. Small remaining-shot numbers and subtle front-row selection corners. This must be visibly a queue, not a card deck or inventory.
- Bottom 91-99%: THREE compact readable rounded buttons with icons and exact Chinese labels: 重排 (shuffle arrows), 优先出战 (forward arrow), 泡泡炸弹 (a small bubble burst icon). Keep the whole game screen visible.

CONSISTENT ORIGINAL CAST: blue #2982F4 round puff with two tiny cheek fins and little feet, big eyes and inflated cheeks; orange #FF7E27 pear-shaped creature with two short rounded horn nubs and a mischievous grin; green #30D183 squat puffy creature with three short soft back bumps, no leaves; purple #B672FD bean-shaped creature with two floppy ear nubs and a broad elastic mouth; yellow #FFDF48 soft rounded-cube creature with two tiny antennae and cheerful face; red #FF525B little inverted-heart creature with a small quiff and energetic determined face. Optional white #FFFFFF round pill creature outlined in cool gray. Each is mostly one main color, tiny simple appendages, no clothes, armor, handheld weapons or large accessories. They visibly inhale, inflate cheeks and spit bubbles with elastic recoil. No generic smiling circles alone: each silhouette and mouth shape has personality.

AVOID: plants, flowers, leaves, vegetables, pots, farm fences, military aircraft, zombies, copied recognizable franchise characters, branded bubble dragons or logos, realistic guns, a single central player cannon, aiming guide lines, finger gesture overlays, match-three exchange arrows, a win popup, tutorial text, extra UI panels, photographic rendering, watermark. All Chinese UI must be crisp and readable.

SCENE 3 — MERGE COMEBACK AT THE BUBBLE CASTLE. Use the attached first image ONLY to keep the same original character designs, art style and UI architecture. A light dusk-lavender bubble castle appears only as tiny inflated turret silhouettes at the far outer corners; never make the game dark or the center busy. Top label 第 76 关, progress 84%. The dense small-bubble mosaic depicts a mischievous purple-and-yellow alien face with blue surround and white eye regions, and its lower front has descended close to the defense rail. The defense rail glows coral red with one modest warning icon, communicating pressure without a popup. Capture the immediate AFTERMATH of three same-purple creatures fusing into ONE larger purple creature on the center pad. The new purple creature has a slightly larger body, puffed cheeks and a small MAX badge at its feet; no weapon or costume. Two neighboring pads are now EMPTY with faint purple residual fusion swirls. Four other occupied pads hold blue, yellow, orange and white allies, keeping exactly FIVE active creatures total and SEVEN pads total. A compact expanding purple circular shockwave just above the pad row pushes the bubble front back visually. The merged purple creature rapidly spits a short dense stream of purple bubbles at a visible exposed purple patch; other allies target their respective colors. Show a local burst and a few dislodged beads, not a giant beam, not a full-screen explosion. Small Chinese callout 三合一 near the fading fusion glow. The drama comes from the frontline nearly touching the rail, two spaces freed by fusion, the bigger purple creature and the upward pushback. Keep four waiting queues and three bottom buttons completely readable.
